ranking_basis: Qualitative expected information gain and practical risk, not numerical leaderboard or holdout predictions. Novelty is limited to targeted searches of this checkout, not the whole registry.

hypotheses.title: Catchment-network knickzone consensus
hypotheses.external_layers: USGS 3DEP elevation tiles and reproducibly derived flow directions, stream topology, and chi. A 5-band chi raster is restored from a hash-pinned owner mirror; the underlying tiles and a channel graph are not.
hypotheses.mechanism: Group tributary knickzones by drainage connectivity, seek coherent chi responses across adjacent catchments, and trace them down actual channels toward a basement/alluvium hinge.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_rationale: A buried range-front scarp could leave a distributed upstream drainage response even where surface mapping misses the fault.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Resistant volcanic or carbonate beds can align knickpoints; drainage capture and erosion thresholds can also mimic the signal.
hypotheses.falsifier_and_novelty: Compare with local-chi and pixel-shift H86T/H86S ablations at matched budget; do not claim graph-level novelty beyond the searched checkout. Mask lithologic contacts and test null catchments. H86T tested pixel-gradient shifts, not a validated stream-network graph.
hypotheses.expected_improvement_rank: 1 — potentially broad, but unknown; no numeric gain or score forecast
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: tile/graph preparation, physical review and spatial holdout; runtime unmeasured.
hypotheses.availability: USGS metadata describes free 3DEP products. The owner-derived 5-band chi raster and 10-m terrain grid were hash- and grid-verified in this review, but exact source tiles, graph, processing and coverage remain unverified.

hypotheses.title: Robust thermal-manifestation corridor graph
hypotheses.external_layers: Hash-verified owner mirrors of GDR 1391 spring/well and volcanic-vent CSVs; additional temperature or paleo-sinter records and a separately sourced road-access control. Exclude dist_known_fault_px and any other fault-derived fields from BOTH CSVs.
hypotheses.mechanism: Test whether several spatially separated, independently sourced thermal-fluid observations form robust line corridors corroborated by magnetic, gravity or surface conductivity edges.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_rationale: A permeable subsurface structure may be obscured by basin fill even where some fluid manifestations exist; truly blind systems can have none, limiting recall.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Road access, exploration siting, playa-margin groundwater and range-front topography can align wells or springs without a fault.
hypotheses.falsifier_and_novelty: Ablate corridor fitting against point-distance features and access-matched random alignments; split by whole districts and source provenance. RANSAC alignment was queued but not located as an executed primary operator in targeted source search.
hypotheses.expected_improvement_rank: 2 — potentially high precision but sparse; no numeric gain or score forecast
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium: data cleaning, source deduplication, access-bias controls and leakage-safe spatial validation; runtime unmeasured.
hypotheses.availability: During this review, owner-mirror spring/well and vent CSVs were hash-verified (27,092 and 21 rows respectively); these counts do not establish coordinate accuracy, deduplication, eligibility or official-source identity. Temperature, paleo-sinter and road-control inputs were not restored or validated.

hypotheses.title: Geodetic–seismic concordance at gravity edges
hypotheses.external_layers: None initially beyond native competition bands; independent earthquake source metadata and observation dates must be established before interpreting Bands 10/16.
hypotheses.mechanism: Seek coincident anisotropic geodetic shear/dilation and earthquake-distance/intensity patterns near a sharp gravity edge, optionally conditioning on surface conductivity without assuming a 2-km MT layer.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_rationale: A diffuse or buried deformation zone may express geodetic and seismic activity without a mapped through-going surface trace.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Induced seismicity, spatially varying detection, interpolation artifacts and nonfault lithologic contacts can produce apparent concordance.
hypotheses.falsifier_and_novelty: Ablate each data group and compare with existing standalone earthquake-lineation and geodetic models; preserve event/district holdouts. The H86T queued label mapping was wrong; this corrected combination has not been verified as executed by the targeted search.
hypotheses.expected_improvement_rank: 3 — coarse observations may not localize the 300-m metric; no numeric gain or score forecast
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low-medium if data semantics are independently established; validation and source-epoch work dominate. Runtime unmeasured.
hypotheses.availability: Native 19-band owner mirror was hash-verified during this review, but the required shared feature-cache identity is unresolved; TIFF headers alone do not validate earthquake semantics.

hypotheses.title: GNSS transient strain-change mapping
hypotheses.external_layers: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory daily GNSS station positions and metadata, with reference-frame, common-mode and instrument-step corrections.
hypotheses.mechanism: Locate spatially coherent, quality-controlled displacement or strain-rate changes and test whether they align with independent subsurface contrasts.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_rationale: An episodically slipping or pressure-responsive structure could be absent from a static surface-fault map.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Groundwater extraction, seasonal loading, equipment changes, common-mode noise and geothermal operations can all imitate transient deformation.
hypotheses.falsifier_and_novelty: Control for known station offsets, seasonal loading and operations; compare static GNSS and leave-station-out baselines. No daily-time-series changepoint ingestion was found in targeted source search.
hypotheses.expected_improvement_rank: 4 — station sparsity and temporal mismatch create high uncertainty; no numeric gain or score forecast
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: station selection, time-series quality control and spatial/temporal validation; runtime unmeasured.
hypotheses.availability: NGL publicly lists daily station products, but exact stations, dates, terms and bytes have not been downloaded or verified in this environment.
